findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on datetime ordering (math.floor on datetime)
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does `int(math.floor(value))` on the raw attribute value, but the only caller (OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint) uses it with `order_by="-datetime"`, so `value` is a `datetime.datetime` and `math.floor()` raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime`. This is exactly why DateTimePaginator exists (it converts the datetime to a millisecond timestamp first). Every request with `optimized_pagination=true` will 500 on the first page when `build_cursor` computes the cursor key. Additionally, `value_from_cursor` returns the raw cursor value, so even past that point the datetime column would be compared against a bare integer timestamp, producing wrong filtering. The optimized path is completely broken for its intended use.

findings.title: Negative-offset 'advanced' path crashes: Django does not support negative queryset slicing
findings.body: The new branch `if self.enable_advanced_features and cursor.offset < 0` slices the queryset with `queryset[start_offset:stop]` where `start_offset = cursor.offset` is negative. The comment claims 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically', which is false: Django's QuerySet slicing raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported.` The cursor offset is attacker/user-controllable via the `cursor` query parameter (e.g. `?cursor=0:-100:0`), so any superuser/admin passing a negative offset with `optimized_pagination=true` gets a 500. The same crash applies in the BasePaginator change at line 182-184, where an `is_prev` cursor with a negative offset is passed through unclamped into the slice.

findings.title: organization_context.member can be None, causing AttributeError for token-based auth
findings.body: The gating expression `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` dereferences `organization_context.member` without a None check. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is None when the request is authenticated with an organization auth token or other non-member credentials (in which case `request.user` is anonymous and `is_superuser` is False, so short-circuiting does not save it). Such requests to the audit log endpoint will now raise AttributeError and return 500 instead of the audit log listing.

findings.title: No tests for OptimizedCursorPaginator or the new endpoint branch
findings.body: The PR adds ~100 lines of new pagination logic (OptimizedCursorPaginator) plus a new conditional branch in the audit log endpoint, but adds no tests. Basic tests exercising `optimized_pagination=true` would have immediately caught the datetime math.floor TypeError and the negative-slicing AssertionError described above. At minimum, tests should cover the happy path with datetime ordering, forward/backward cursor navigation, and rejection/clamping of negative-offset cursors.

findings.title: Misleading comments justify broken negative-offset behavior
findings.body: New comments in cursors.py and paginator.py claim that negative offsets are a safe 'performance optimization' and that 'the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions' / 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically'. These statements are incorrect — Django explicitly rejects negative queryset indexing — and the comments serve to rationalize code paths that crash at runtime. The comments should be removed or corrected along with the broken code.
